title: E = mc²: Mass Is Energy
hook: The most famous equation in physics says mass and energy are the same thing. Because the speed of light squared is a colossal number, a tiny bit of mass holds a staggering amount of energy.
key_points: Mass and energy are two forms of one thing; mass can convert to energy and back.
The c² factor is enormous, so even a minuscule mass packs immense energy.
The Sun shines by turning a little of its mass into energy through fusion.
Nuclear power and weapons release this locked-in mass-energy.
content_html: In 1905 Einstein drew a startling conclusion from his theory of relativity: mass and energy are not separate quantities but the same thing wearing different clothes. The equation E = mc² ties them together, with c the speed of light. Because c is about 300,000 kilometers per second, c² is an astronomically large number — which means a very small amount of mass is equivalent to an enormous amount of energy.
extra_html: The practical upshot is everywhere. The Sun shines because, deep in its core, hydrogen fuses into helium and the helium weighs a touch less than the hydrogen that made it; that vanished mass streams out as sunlight. Nuclear reactors and weapons tap the same bank, converting a sliver of mass in heavy atoms into heat and radiation. Even an ordinary chemical fire converts a truly tiny bit of mass to energy, far too little to notice. The equation also runs the other way: smash particles together hard enough and their energy of motion can congeal into brand-new particles with real mass, which is what happens inside accelerators. Wikipedia lays out the equation's meaning and its many confirmations.

related.title: Special Relativity, Gently
related.hook: Einstein started with one strange fact — light's speed is the same for everyone — and out fell that time itself can stretch.

related.title: What Powers the Sun
related.hook: The Sun isn't burning like a fire — it's fusing hydrogen into helium in its core, and a sliver of mass turning into pure energy is what lights up our sky.

related.title: Nuclear Fission
related.hook: Split one heavy nucleus and it releases neutrons that split more — a chain reaction that, tamed, lights cities, and unleashed, levels them.

related.title: Nuclear Fusion
related.hook: The same reaction that powers every star — squeezing light nuclei together — could one day give Earth nearly limitless clean energy, if we can hold a sun in a box.

flashcards.prompt: What does E = mc² actually claim about mass and energy?
flashcards.back_html: They're the same thing in two forms. Mass is a hugely concentrated store of energy, and a small mass can convert into a large amount of energy.

flashcards.prompt: Why does a tiny amount of mass correspond to so much energy?

choices.text: The conversion factor is c², the speed of light squared — an enormous number
Mass is multiplied by the object's temperature
Energy grows with how heavy the object feels on Earth

flashcards.explanation_html: Light moves at about 300,000 km/s, so c² is gigantic. Multiplying even a gram of mass by it gives a vast energy.

flashcards.prompt: How does E = mc² explain why the Sun shines?

choices.text: Fusion converts a small fraction of the Sun's mass into radiated energy
The Sun burns hydrogen like a chemical fire
Sunlight is stored mass slowly leaking out unchanged

flashcards.explanation_html: In the Sun's core, hydrogen fuses into helium; the products weigh slightly less than the ingredients, and that missing mass leaves as energy.
